# chdzip

[← Command index](README.md)

Repack the files on each CHD disc image into a zip archive.

## Synopsis

```
chdzip [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.chd` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and turns
the filesystem on the disc into `<name>.zip` next to it. chdman extracts the disc to
`<name>.iso` and `<name>.toc` beside the CHD, the ISO is mounted on a temporary
directory (with fuseiso on Linux), and 7-Zip archives the mounted files.

A CHD whose `<name>.zip` already exists is skipped.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | A `.chd` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |
| `-d, --delete_originals` | Delete each CHD after its zip is written. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Zip the contents of every CHD in a folder

```bash
chdzip -i /path/to/chds
```

### Zip and delete the CHDs, previewing first

```bash
chdzip -i /path/to/chds -d -p -v
```

## Notes

- Only the files in the disc's filesystem go into the zip, not the disc image itself.
- The extracted ISO sits next to the CHD, so that directory needs room for a full copy of the disc.
- chdman (MameChdman) and 7-Zip must be installed as JoyBox tools, and on Linux fuseiso as well.
